extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in economics/finance, patent analytics, and machine learning (academic and industry) interested in patent valuation and acceptance prediction
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating machine-learning models (LLM embeddings + structural features) to predict USPTO patent application acceptance and the economic value of patents (KPSS measure), and using those predictions for screening, valuation adjustment, and portfolio strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and sample selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary data from USPTO PatentsView (applications from 2001) and USPTO BDSS for full text, supplemented by CRSP/Compustat (WRDS) for market data; sample restricted to observations with a valid assignee 'permno' and observations with multiple assignees dropped to avoid duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final sample contains applications and patents from 2001–2020 (applications effectively tested 2004–2019); exclude 2021–2022 due to truncation and exclude 2020 because pandemic introduced new trends not present in training; use rolling-window training (models trained on the three preceding years) to maintain contextual relevance and avoid using unavailable future information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual embedding input (Ada-002, 1536-dim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine title and abstract of each application/patent and feed through OpenAI's Ada-002 embedding model to obtain a 1,536-dimensional numeric vector representing many textual aspects (sentiment, topic, writing quality, technicality, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The embedding supplies rich high-level textual features previously inaccessible; use embedding as part of the feature vector alongside structural variables rather than as sole input unless intentionally isolating text effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural variables to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Include CPC classification (Class A,B,C,...), USPTO-generated AI patent measure, industry flags (ICT, biotechnology, high tech) defined via EU classification, number of CPC classes, ln(number of claims), research-institution assignee flag, and Fama-French 12 industry classification. For application prediction, include natural log of market capitalization (nearest quarter prior to publication, inflation-adjusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural/contextual variables provide critical context for textual embeddings and should be combined with the embedding vector in the feature matrix; omit variables not available in processed PatentView application data when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For acceptance prediction, dependent is a binary dummy equal to 1 if application is granted as a patent and 0 if rejected. For value prediction, use the KPSS measure (market reaction to announcement of patent acceptance in a three-day window), scaled by market capitalization as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent calculation of KPSS per the KPSS (2017) procedure and the correct timing of market-cap and return data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training regime: rolling three-year window
rubrics_metrics.description: Train predictive models using a rolling window composed of the three preceding years for the year being predicted (e.g., model for 2004 trained on 2001–2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents look-ahead bias, ensures contextual relevance for temporal trends, and maintains a sufficiently large training sample for deep learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling skewness in acceptance prediction: optimize binary cross-entropy (log-loss)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the acceptance dependent is heavily skewed (~70% grants), optimize the model for binary cross-entropy rather than raw accuracy or F1 to adapt to class imbalance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimizing for Accuracy or F1 tends to bias models toward the null predictor in skewed samples; use log-loss and AUC for better discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for binary classification (preference for AUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report AUC (area under ROC) as the primary evaluation metric for acceptance prediction, and also report Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AUC is preferred due to sample skewness because it measures ranking performance and is less fooled by the null predictor; Accuracy and F1 can be deceptively similar across models that actually differ in ranking (AUC). Provide year-by-year statistics and averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark the primary model (embedding + structural features in advanced deep network) against: (1) an otherwise identical neural network trained without the textual embedding features, and (2) an XGBoost model trained on the full set of features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons should include the same evaluation metrics (AUC, Accuracy, F1, etc.) to quantify the incremental value of the embedding and the chosen network architecture; also test simpler classifiers (e.g., linear SVC) though they may fail in high-dimensional settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural network architecture (three-layer MLP with geometric node counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feed the 1,536-dim embedding plus structural variables into a three-layer feed-forward neural network (multi-layer perceptron) with node counts set as a roughly geometric series; final layer has no activation (linear output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the penultimate layer to produce an output that OLS-like regression can act upon; include implementation details (Appendix A) and ensure architecture supports high-dimensional embedding interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation function choice: use Mish
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Mish activation function (Mish(x) = x * tanh(ln(1 + e^x))) as the primary activation for hidden layers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mish was found to perform significantly better in large-sample, high-feature-count settings versus ReLU, ELU, or Swish, likely due to better handling of negative inputs and capturing non-linear interactions; still compare alternatives where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularization: 20% dropout preferred over L1/L2
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply dropout regularization at 20% to prevent overfitting, which outperformed L1 and L2 regularization in maintaining high-degree interactions within the embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dropout helps avoid near-interpolation of the training sample and reduces overfitting while preserving complex embedding interactions; test and report robustness versus other regularizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimizer: Adam
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Adam optimizer to train the neural networks, which parametrizes learning rate for improved convergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune learning-rate-related hyperparameters as needed; Adam is a default proven choice for such networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value prediction: dependent transformation via Box–Cox
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform highly skewed KPSS patent-value dependent using Box–Cox (compute λ on training set only), as Box–Cox outperformed ln(1+y), quantile normal, and standardization for improving R-squared in ML models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute λ only on the training set and apply the same transformation to test data to avoid contaminating test statistics; transforming the dependent stabilizes variance and improves ML predictive performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model comparison metric for value prediction: adjusted R-squared
rubrics_metrics.description: Use adjusted R-squared as a primary performance metric for value prediction (model achieved ~42% adjusted R-squared; embedding adds ~24% improvement over no-embedding benchmark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report MSE, R2, and adjusted R2 year-by-year and averaged; compare to XGBoost and no-embedding baselines to show incremental gains from embedding and architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude variables unavailable in processed PatentView application data from application prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Omit variables not present in PatentView's processed application data (example: number of claims and an AI classification variable) from the application prediction feature set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document excluded variables explicitly and explain potential impacts on comparability; ensure fairness in benchmarking models by using features actually available at prediction time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring text change between application and grant via embedding cosine distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the magnitude of textual change between application and granted-patent abstracts using cosine distance between their ChatGPT embeddings; a major change is defined as cosine distance ≥ 0.05 (also tested with threshold 0.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embedding-based semantic distance rather than crude text-difference measures (character changes); selecting thresholds (0.05, 0.02) influences subsample size and statistical power — report robustness to threshold choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application screening workflow (practical procedure for firms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce an intermediate screening step where firms iteratively run prospective applications through the acceptance model, revise the text until a satisfactory acceptance-probability threshold is reached, and optionally apply the value model to balance acceptance probability and expected market reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening is especially valuable for startups and small firms lacking patent-law expertise; firms should monitor revisions using the embedding distance metric and consider both acceptance and predicted value rather than acceptance alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing firm-level application strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Define application strength for a firm-month as the mean predicted chance of acceptance for all the firm's applications published that month, multiplied by the square root of the number of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measure proxies both the average quality and the scale of firm application activity; use it for firm sorting in portfolio analysis and as a latent indicator of innovative strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio construction and evaluation using application-strength signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort firms monthly into above- vs. below-median application-strength groups; construct a long-short portfolio (long high-strength, short low-strength) with a one-month horizon and evaluate abnormal returns using Fama-French three-, four-, and five-factor regressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report monthly and annualized abnormal returns and significance (one-tailed t-tests); the paper finds significant annual abnormal returns (~3.3% yearly) for portfolios based on application strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability caution and qualitative validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that there are no consistent, general methods for global interpretation of neural networks; use qualitative inspection and case studies (e.g., unreadable or repetitive abstracts flagged as low-quality) to validate model intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement quantitative metrics with manual review of extreme predictions (top/bottom predicted applications) to identify textual patterns (vague, repetitive, or unclear writing) driving model outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of statistical contamination when transforming dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying transformations like Box–Cox, calculate transformation parameters (λ) only on the training set and then apply them to the test set to avoid invalidating statistical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report robustness checks demonstrating that training-only λ yields similar results to in-sample λ when sample sizes are large, and document the procedure clearly in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular reporting of year-by-year performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report model evaluation metrics (AUC, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 for acceptance; MSE, R2, adjusted R2 for value) on a year-by-year basis and present means/medians across years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal reporting reveals trends (e.g., increasing R2 over time) and indicates whether market incorporation or model performance is improving; include tables for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of LLM-based patent evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs currently lack robust symbolic processing and are not qualified to evaluate engineering or design quality; models likely capture writing quality and self-reported importance rather than deep scientific inventiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat model outputs as proxies for perceived application quality or market-signaling content; anticipate future improvements from multimodal models (figures/drawings) and exercise caution in consequential decisions relying solely on text embeddings.
